#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render text with a font to PNG using uharfbuzz (shaping) + freetype (rasterize).

Used to proof both reference fonts and the font built by this project.
"""
import argparse
import sys

import uharfbuzz as hb
import freetype
from PIL import Image


def load_hb_font(path, size):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    face = hb.Face(data)
    font = hb.Font(face)
    upem = face.upem
    font.scale = (size * 64, size * 64)  # 26.6 fixed point
    hb.ot_font_set_funcs(font)
    return font, upem


def shape(font, text):
    buf = hb.Buffer()
    buf.add_str(text)
    buf.guess_segment_properties()
    hb.shape(font, buf)
    infos = buf.glyph_infos
    positions = buf.glyph_positions
    return list(zip(infos, positions))


def render_alpha(font_path, text, size=64, pad=20, show_baseline=False):
    """Render text to a grayscale image (255 = ink) and return (image, baseline)."""
    hbfont, upem = load_hb_font(font_path, size)
    ftface = freetype.Face(font_path)
    ftface.set_char_size(size * 64)

    shaped = shape(hbfont, text)
    pen_x = 0.0
    top_max = 0.0
    bottom_max = 0.0
    glyphs = []
    for info, pos in shaped:
        gid = info.codepoint
        x_adv = pos.x_advance / 64.0
        x_off = pos.x_offset / 64.0
        y_off = pos.y_offset / 64.0
        ftface.load_glyph(gid, freetype.FT_LOAD_RENDER | freetype.FT_LOAD_TARGET_NORMAL)
        bitmap = ftface.glyph.bitmap
        left = ftface.glyph.bitmap_left
        top = ftface.glyph.bitmap_top
        w, rows, pitch = bitmap.width, bitmap.rows, bitmap.pitch
        data = bytes(bitmap.buffer) if (w and rows) else b""
        gx = pen_x + x_off + left
        top_above = top + y_off
        bottom_below = rows - top - y_off
        top_max = max(top_max, top_above)
        bottom_max = max(bottom_max, bottom_below)
        glyphs.append((data, w, rows, pitch, gx, top, y_off))
        pen_x += x_adv

    width = int(pen_x) + 2 * pad
    height = int(top_max + bottom_max) + 2 * pad
    if width <= 0 or height <= 0:
        return None, 0
    img = Image.new("L", (width, height), 0)
    baseline_y = pad + top_max
    for data, w, rows, pitch, gx, top, y_off in glyphs:
        px = int(round(gx)) + pad
        py = int(round(baseline_y - top - y_off))
        if w == 0 or rows == 0:
            continue
        stride = abs(pitch) if pitch else w
        glyph_img = Image.new("L", (w, rows), 0)
        gp = glyph_img.load()
        for r in range(rows):
            base = r * stride
            for c in range(w):
                v = data[base + c]
                if v:
                    gp[c, r] = v
        img.paste(glyph_img, (px, py), glyph_img)
    if show_baseline:
        from PIL import ImageDraw
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
        d.line([(0, int(baseline_y)), (width, int(baseline_y))], fill=128, width=1)
    return img, baseline_y


def render(font_path, text, out_path, size=64, pad=20, fg=(30, 30, 30), bg=(255, 255, 255), show_baseline=False):
    hbfont, upem = load_hb_font(font_path, size)
    ftface = freetype.Face(font_path)
    ftface.set_char_size(size * 64)

    shaped = shape(hbfont, text)

    # Single pass: load each glyph, snapshot its pixels immediately (freetype
    # reuses the glyph slot, so we must copy the buffer right away).
    pen_x = 0.0
    top_max = 0.0      # max distance of glyph-top above baseline
    bottom_max = 0.0   # max distance of glyph-bottom below baseline
    glyphs = []
    for info, pos in shaped:
        gid = info.codepoint
        x_adv = pos.x_advance / 64.0
        x_off = pos.x_offset / 64.0
        y_off = pos.y_offset / 64.0  # positive = up

        ftface.load_glyph(gid, freetype.FT_LOAD_RENDER | freetype.FT_LOAD_TARGET_NORMAL)
        bitmap = ftface.glyph.bitmap
        left = ftface.glyph.bitmap_left
        top = ftface.glyph.bitmap_top  # px of bitmap top above baseline
        w, rows, pitch = bitmap.width, bitmap.rows, bitmap.pitch
        data = bytes(bitmap.buffer) if (w and rows) else b""

        gx = pen_x + x_off + left          # x of bitmap left edge
        top_above = top + y_off            # glyph top above baseline
        bottom_below = rows - top - y_off  # glyph bottom below baseline
        top_max = max(top_max, top_above)
        bottom_max = max(bottom_max, bottom_below)
        glyphs.append((data, w, rows, pitch, gx, top, y_off))
        pen_x += x_adv

    width = int(pen_x) + 2 * pad
    height = int(top_max + bottom_max) + 2 * pad
    if width <= 0 or height <= 0:
        print("nothing to render", file=sys.stderr)
        return

    img = Image.new("RGB", (width, height), bg)
    baseline_y = pad + top_max  # baseline position in image coords

    for data, w, rows, pitch, gx, top, y_off in glyphs:
        px = int(round(gx)) + pad
        py = int(round(baseline_y - top - y_off))
        if w == 0 or rows == 0:
            continue
        stride = abs(pitch) if pitch else w
        glyph_img = Image.new("L", (w, rows), 0)
        gp = glyph_img.load()
        for r in range(rows):
            base = r * stride
            for c in range(w):
                v = data[base + c]
                if v:
                    gp[c, r] = v
        img.paste(fg, (px, py), glyph_img)

    if show_baseline:
        from PIL import ImageDraw
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
        d.line([(0, int(baseline_y)), (width, int(baseline_y))], fill=(255, 0, 0), width=1)

    img.save(out_path)
    print(f"wrote {out_path}  ({width}x{height})  glyphs={len(glyphs)}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("font")
    ap.add_argument("text")
    ap.add_argument("out")
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    render(args.font, args.text, args.out, size=args.size, show_baseline=args.baseline)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text: Can we make whatever we are building as: Manjari Derivative, like the previous font:

Manjari itself only contains **Malayalam + Latin** — it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada glyphs. So a literal “Manjari derivative” can cover the Malayalam branch, but the other four scripts need their own OFL skeleton. I can still keep the exact same derivative model, naming, attribution and aperture engine.

I prototyped the four scripts on Noto Sans skeletons. Early results:

- **Telugu / Kannada** — the full petal warp works beautifully on their round loops.
- **Devanagari** — the full warp bends the headline; a counters-only profile keeps the shirorekha straight and turns the counters into lotus windows.
- **Tamil** — needs a gentler profile; the full warp makes the open tops too spiky.

How should I proceed?

def warp(font, hole_bump=110, peak_bump=40, sigma_f=0.28, pinch=0.055, cap_frac=0.55, top_frac=1.0, freeze_top=False, valley_bump=0):
    glyf=font['glyf']
    for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
        if gname not in glyf: continue
        glyph=glyf[gname]
        if getattr(glyph,'numberOfContours',0)<=0: continue
        coords=glyph.coordinates; new=copy.deepcopy(coords)
        contours=_split_contours(glyph); allpts=[coords[i] for i in range(len(coords))]
        gymin=min(p[1] for p in allpts); gymax=max(p[1] for p in allpts); gh=max(1.0,gymax-gymin)
        cutoff=gymin+top_frac*gh
        outer_pts=[]
        for s,e in contours:
            pts=[coords[i] for i in range(s,e+1)]
            if contour_area(pts)<0: outer_pts.extend(pts)
        tree=cKDTree(outer_pts) if outer_pts else None
        for s,e in contours:
            pts=[coords[i] for i in range(s,e+1)]; ar=contour_area(pts)
            xmin=min(p[0] for p in pts); xmax=max(p[0] for p in pts)
            ymin=min(p[1] for p in pts); ymax=max(p[1] for p in pts)
            cx=(xmin+xmax)/2; w=max(1.0,(xmax-xmin)/2); h=ymax-ymin
            if ar>0:
                if h<=20 or w<=20 or tree is None: continue
                for i in range(s,e+1):

                    u=(x-cx)/w; v=(y-ymin)/h
                    if v<=0.45: continue
                    t=(v-0.45)/0.55; dist=tree.query((x,y))[0]
                    bump=min(hole_bump,cap_frac*dist); pin=min(pinch*w,0.30*dist)
                    new[i]=(x-pin*u*t*t, y+bump*(1-u*u)*t*t)
            else:
                n=len(pts); peaks=[]
                for j in range(n):
                    y0=pts[(j-1)%n][1]; y1=pts[j][1]; y2=pts[(j+1)%n][1]
                    if y1>=y0 and y1>=y2 and y1>gymin+0.45*gh:
                        if y1>cutoff: continue

def instantiate(src, dst, location):
    font = TTFont(src)
    instantiateVariableFont(font, location, inplace=True)
    font.save(dst)
    return font


def instantiate_with_names(src, dst, location, family, style):
    font = TTFont(src)
    instantiateVariableFont(font, location, inplace=True)
    # drop variation tables left over from the instancer
    for tag in ("fvar", "gvar", "STAT", "avar", "HVAR"):
        if tag in font:
            del font[tag]
    set_names(font, family, style, weight=700 if "Bold" in style else 400)
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(dst)
    return font


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("command", nargs="?", default="all",
                    choices=["masters", "variable", "spectrum", "instances", "all"])
    ap.add_argument("--proof", action="store_true",
                    help="also render proof PNGs (slow)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    os.makedirs(MASTERS, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FONTS, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(PROOFS, exist_ok=True)

    reg_petal = os.path.join(MASTERS, "Kamalam-Regular-Petal.ttf")
    bold_round = os.path.join(MASTERS, "Kamalam-Bold-Round.ttf")
    bold_petal = os.path.join(MASTERS, "Kamalam-Bold-Petal.ttf")

    if args.command in ("masters", "all"):
        normalize(os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Regular.ttf"), reg_round,
                  petal=False, weight=400, style="Regular")
        normalize(os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Regular.ttf"), reg_petal,
                  petal=True, weight=400, style="Regular")
        normalize(os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Bold.ttf"), bold_round,
                  petal=False, weight=700, style="Bold")
        normalize(os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Bold.ttf"), bold_petal,
                  petal=True, weight=700, style="Bold")
        print("masters written to", MASTERS)

    reg_ds = os.path.join(MASTERS, "Kamalam-Regular.designspace")
    bold_ds = os.path.join(MASTERS, "Kamalam-Bold.designspace")
    if args.command in ("variable", "all"):
        build_designspace(reg_round, reg_petal, reg_ds, style="Regular")
        build_designspace(bold_round, bold_petal, bold_ds, style="Bold")
        reg_vf = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf")
        bold_vf = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Bold.ttf")
        build_vf(reg_ds, reg_vf, style="Regular")
        build_vf(bold_ds, bold_vf, style="Bold")
        print("variable fonts written to", FONTS)

    if args.command in ("spectrum", "all"):
        reg_vf = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf")
        bold_vf = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Bold.ttf")
        spectrum = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Spectrum.ttf")
        spectrum_reg = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-SpectrumRegular.ttf")
        add_spectrum(bold_vf, spectrum, style="Bold", weight=700)
        add_spectrum(reg_vf, spectrum_reg, style="Regular", weight=400)

    if args.command in ("instances", "all"):
        reg_vf = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf")

        instantiate_with_names(reg_vf, os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Round.ttf"),
                               {"APER": 0}, "Ezhuthu Kamalam Round", "Regular")
        instantiate_with_names(reg_vf, os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Petal.ttf"),
                               {"APER": 100}, "Ezhuthu Kamalam Petal", "Regular")
        instantiate_with_names(bold_vf, os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-BoldPetal.ttf"),
                               {"APER": 100}, "Ezhuthu Kamalam Petal", "Bold")
        print("static instances written")

    # WOFF2 for every TTF in fonts/ root

        src = os.path.join(FONTS, fn)

# Base skeletons

Ezhuthu Kamalam is a multi-script type system built on open-source structural
skeletons. The new work is the aperture engine (`APER`), the lotus-gateway
counters, the Spectrum builds, the metrics, the build pipeline and the
specimens. The base outlines are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

| Branch | Upstream | Vendored file | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Malayalam | [Manjari](https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari) by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC | `Manjari-Regular.ttf`, `Manjari-Bold.ttf` | see `AUTHORS.md` |
| Devanagari | [Noto Sans Devanagari](https://github.com/notofonts/devanagari) | `NotoSansDevanagari-VF.ttf` | `14ec4af41f27482216d1c2229f417ff9b1425e1babb014e57d1d40d03229853e` |
| Tamil | [Noto Sans Tamil](https://github.com/notofonts/tamil) | `NotoSansTamil-VF.ttf` | `aa3a9b321f4b0bb2c40203ffbde9af89713227866e0e13f76e5b9eeea727cf88` |
| Telugu | [Noto Sans Telugu](https://github.com/notofonts/telugu) | `NotoSansTelugu-VF.ttf` | `e618af7bf999df192ed4f388eba2e563f2b5015034e9cbb317b5bd793bd7334d` |
| Kannada | [Noto Sans Kannada](https://github.com/notofonts/kannada) | `NotoSansKannada-VF.ttf` | `cca4f3b3a8cb12fb261f1b43baf5d2f7f59d90fe123d41f0065ed3a183997ec9` |

The Noto variable fonts were downloaded from the `google/fonts` repository on
2026-11-09. They are vendored so that builds are offline and reproducible.
Each upstream font carries its own copyright notice in its `name` table and
its own `OFL.txt` beside the binary.

## Derivative model

The Malayalam branch is a derivative of Manjari. The Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu
and Kannada branches are derivatives of the corresponding Noto Sans faces.
Each derived family is renamed to `Ezhuthu Kamalam <Script>`, preserves the
upstream copyright and OFL notice, and records the base in its name table and
documentation. The aperture axis and the Spectrum treatment are original work
by the Ezhuthu Project Authors.

This project is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google,
the Noto Project Authors, Sarvam AI, or SMC.

        for text in CASES:

            if not names or ".notdef" in names:

def petal_warp(font: TTFont, hole_bump=HOLE_BUMP, peak_bump=PEAK_BUMP,
               sigma_f=SIGMA_F, pinch=PINCH, cap_frac=CAP_FRAC,
               only=None, freeze_top=None, peak_max_frac=None,
               valley_bump=0.0):
    """Move counters and outer crowns into lotus-petal shapes.

    The operation is point-preserving: only coordinates change, so two
    masters warped with different parameters remain interpolation-compatible.

    ``only`` restricts the transform to a set of glyph names.  ``freeze_top``
    is a fraction of the glyph height: points above that line do not move, which
    keeps a headline (Devanagari shirorekha) perfectly straight.  ``peak_max_frac``
    limits outer-contour peak candidates to below that height.  ``valley_bump``
    optionally pulls rounded lower loops into downward petals.
    """
    glyf = font["glyf"]
    for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
        if only is not None and gname not in only:
            continue
        if gname not in glyf:
            continue
        glyph = glyf[gname]
        if glyph.numberOfContours <= 0:
            continue
        coords = glyph.coordinates
        new = copy.deepcopy(coords)
        contours = _split_contours(glyph)
        allpts = [coords[i] for i in range(len(coords))]
        gymin = min(p[1] for p in allpts)
        gymax = max(p[1] for p in allpts)
        gh = max(1.0, gymax - gymin)
        freeze_y = None
        if freeze_top is not None:
            freeze_y = gymin + freeze_top * gh

        # All outer-contour points, used to cap counter movement so a petal
        # can never break through the stroke.
        outer_pts = []
        for s, e in contours:
            pts = [coords[i] for i in range(s, e + 1)]
            if contour_area(pts) < 0:
                outer_pts.extend(pts)
        tree = cKDTree(outer_pts) if outer_pts else None

        for s, e in contours:
            pts = [coords[i] for i in range(s, e + 1)]
            ar = contour_area(pts)
            xmin = min(p[0] for p in pts)
            xmax = max(p[0] for p in pts)
            ymin = min(p[1] for p in pts)
            ymax = max(p[1] for p in pts)
            cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2.0
            w = max(1.0, (xmax - xmin) / 2.0)
            h = ymax - ymin

            if ar > 0:  # counter
                if h <= 20 or w <= 20 or tree is None:
                    continue
                for i in range(s, e + 1):
                    x, y = coords[i]
                    if freeze_y is not None and y > freeze_y:
                        continue
                    u = (x - cx) / w
                    v = (y - ymin) / h
                    if v <= 0.45:
                        continue
                    t = (v - 0.45) / 0.55
                    dist = tree.query((x, y))[0]
                    bump = min(hole_bump, cap_frac * dist)
                    pin = min(pinch * w, 0.30 * dist)
                    new[i] = (x - pin * u * t * t,
                              y + bump * (1.0 - u * u) * t * t)
            else:  # outer contour: sharpen local crowns
                n = len(pts)
                peaks = []
                for j in range(n):
                    y0 = pts[(j - 1) % n][1]
                    y1 = pts[j][1]
                    y2 = pts[(j + 1) % n][1]
                    if y1 >= y0 and y1 >= y2 and y1 > gymin + 0.45 * gh:
                        if (peak_max_frac is not None and
                                y1 > gymin + peak_max_frac * gh):
                            continue
                        if (not peaks or

                            peaks.append((pts[j][0], y1))
                for px, py in peaks:
                    sigma = max(30.0, (xmax - xmin) * sigma_f)
                    for i in range(s, e + 1):
                        x, y = coords[i]
                        if freeze_y is not None and y > freeze_y:
                            continue
                        wy = max(0.0, (y - (gymin + 0.35 * gh)) / (gh * 0.65))
                        wy = min(1.0, wy)
                        d = (x - px) / sigma
                        pull = math.exp(-d * d) * (wy * wy)
                        new[i] = (new[i][0] - 0.5 * pinch * (x - px) * math.exp(-d * d) * wy,
                                  new[i][1] + peak_bump * pull)

                if valley_bump:
                    valleys = []
                    for j in range(n):
                        y0 = pts[(j - 1) % n][1]
                        y1 = pts[j][1]
                        y2 = pts[(j + 1) % n][1]
                        if y1 < y0 and y1 < y2 and y1 < gymin + 0.55 * gh:
                            if (not valleys or
                                    abs(pts[j][0] - valleys[-1][0]) >
                                    0.15 * (xmax - xmin)):
                                valleys.append((pts[j][0], y1))
                    for px, py in valleys:
                        sigma = max(30.0, (xmax - xmin) * sigma_f)
                        for i in range(s, e + 1):
                            x, y = coords[i]
                            if freeze_y is not None and y > freeze_y:
                                continue
                            wy = max(0.0, (gymin + 0.55 * gh - y) / (0.55 * gh))
                            wy = min(1.0, wy)
                            d = (x - px) / sigma
                            pull = math.exp(-d * d) * (wy * wy)
                            new[i] = (new[i][0] - 0.5 * pinch * (x - px) *
                                      math.exp(-d * d) * wy,
                                      new[i][1] - valley_bump * pull)
        glyph.coordinates = new
        glyph.recalcBounds(glyf)

def set_metrics(font: TTFont, weight=400, asc=None, desc=None,
                win_asc=None, win_desc=None, auto_win=False,
                underline_position=None, underline_thickness=None):
    os2 = font["OS/2"]
    hhea = font["hhea"]
    head = font["head"]
    head.fontRevision = 1.0
    head.created = FIXED_TIME
    head.modified = FIXED_TIME
    # Minimal smart-dropout prep.  The font has no TT hinting otherwise;
    # this keeps legacy rasterizers on the smart-dropout path.
    from fontTools.ttLib.tables import ttProgram
    from fontTools.ttLib import newTable
    prep = newTable("prep")
    prep.program = ttProgram.Program()
    prep.program.fromBytecode(bytes([
        0xB8, 0x01, 0xFF, 0x85,  # PUSHW 0x01FF; SCANCTRL
        0xB0, 0x04, 0x8D,        # PUSHB 0x04; SCANTYPE
    ]))
    font["prep"] = prep
    asc = 800 if asc is None else asc
    desc = -300 if desc is None else desc
    if auto_win:
        glyf = font["glyf"]
        extents = []
        for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
            if gname not in glyf:
                continue
            g = glyf[gname]
            if getattr(g, "numberOfContours", 0) == 0:
                continue
            extents.append((g.yMin, g.yMax))
        ymin = min(e[0] for e in extents)
        ymax = max(e[1] for e in extents)
        win_asc = max(asc, int(math.ceil(ymax)) + 50)
        win_desc = max(-desc, int(math.ceil(-ymin)) + 50)
    else:
        win_asc = 1100 if win_asc is None else win_asc
        win_desc = 700 if win_desc is None else win_desc
    os2.sTypoAscender = asc
    os2.sTypoDescender = desc
    os2.sTypoLineGap = 0
    os2.usWinAscent = win_asc
    os2.usWinDescent = win_desc
    os2.usWeightClass = weight
    os2.achVendID = "EZHX"
    os2.fsSelection = (os2.fsSelection & ~0x21) | (0x20 if weight >= 700 else 0x40)

    hhea.ascent = asc

    hhea.lineGap = 0

    # neutral, upright font
    font["post"].italicAngle = 0.0
    font["post"].underlinePosition = (

    )
    font["post"].underlineThickness = (
        50 if underline_thickness is None else underline_thickness
    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ezhuthu Kamalam multiscript — Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada.

The Malayalam family is built by ``tools/kamalam.py`` from Manjari.  This
module builds the sister families from the corresponding Noto Sans variable
skeletons, applying the same ``APER`` aperture engine, naming model, Spectrum
treatment and QA pipeline.

Each family is a separate variable font because the scripts have different
shaping tables, glyph sets and vertical metrics.  They share the APER axis
(0..100, default 100), the five named stops, the Spectrum palette and the
static Round/Petal instances, so they can be used together as one type system.

Usage:
    python tools/multiscript.py                 # all four scripts
    python tools/multiscript.py devanagari      # one script
    python tools/multiscript.py tamil telugu    # a subset

The build is deterministic: the base fonts are vendored, the timestamps are
pinned and the transform only moves existing TrueType points, so repeated runs
produce byte-identical files.

import sys

from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont

    FIXED_TIME,

)

PROJECT_URL = "https://github.com/kurianbenoy/ezhuthu"

NOTO_TAML = "https://github.com/notofonts/tamil"
NOTO_TELU = "https://github.com/notofonts/telugu"
NOTO_KNDA = "https://github.com/notofonts/kannada"

SCRIPTS = {

# Tables that cannot survive a change of outlines / instancing.
DROP_TABLES = (
    "fvar", "gvar", "avar", "STAT", "HVAR", "MVAR", "VVAR", "DSIG",
    "prep", "fpgm", "cvt ", "VDMX", "hdmx", "LTSH",
)


def script_codepoints(font, ranges):
    cps = set()
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if not table.isUnicode():
            continue
        for cp in table.cmap:
            if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in ranges):
                cps.add(cp)
    return cps


def script_glyphs(path, codepoints):
    """Return the GSUB closure of a script's codepoints.

    Using fontTools' subsetter closure means conjuncts, half forms, reph forms
    and contextual variants are all included, while Latin, punctuation and
    unrelated glyphs are left in the base style.
    """
    font = TTFont(path)
    opts = subset.Options()
    opts.layout_features = ["*"]
    opts.notdef_outline = True
    opts.recalc_bounds = False
    opts.drop_tables = []
    subsetter = subset.Subsetter(opts)
    subsetter.populate(unicodes=codepoints)
    subsetter.subset(font)
    names = set(font.getGlyphOrder())
    names.discard(".notdef")
    return names


def copyright_for(script):
    return (
        f"Copyright 2022 The Noto Project Authors ({script['upstream']}). "
        "Modified 2026 by The Ezhuthu Project Authors. "
        "Licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1."
    )


def designer_for(_script):
    return "Ezhuthu Project Authors; base design by the Noto Project Authors"


def style_for(weight):
    return "Regular" if weight == 400 else "Bold"


def instantiate_base(script, weight):
    out = os.path.join(
        MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style_for(weight)}-Round.ttf"
    )
    font = TTFont(script["base"])
    instantiateVariableFont(font, {"wght": weight, "wdth": 100}, inplace=True)
    for tag in DROP_TABLES:
        if tag in font:
            del font[tag]
    scale_upem(font, UPEM)
    style = style_for(weight)
    set_names(
        font, script["family"], style, weight=weight,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script),
        url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    set_metrics(font, weight=weight, **script["metrics"])
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(out)
    return out


def make_petal(round_path, petal_path, glyphs, warp):
    font = TTFont(round_path)
    petal_warp(font, only=glyphs, **warp)
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(petal_path)
    return petal_path


def to_woff2(path):
    font = TTFont(path)
    font.flavor = "woff2"
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(path[:-4] + ".woff2")
    return path[:-4] + ".woff2"


def build_script(key):
    script = SCRIPTS[key]
    os.makedirs(MASTERS, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FONTS, exist_ok=True)

    paths = []
    vfs = {}
    for weight in (400, 700):
        style = style_for(weight)
        round_path = instantiate_base(script, weight)
        if weight == 400:
            cps = script_codepoints(TTFont(round_path), script["ranges"])
            glyphs = script_glyphs(round_path, cps)
            print(f"{key}: {len(cps)} codepoints, {len(glyphs)} glyphs in closure")
        petal_path = os.path.join(
            MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}-Petal.ttf"
        )
        make_petal(round_path, petal_path, glyphs, script["warp"])
        ds_path = os.path.join(MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.designspace")
        build_designspace(
            round_path, petal_path, ds_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
        )
        vf_path = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.ttf")
        build_vf(
            ds_path, vf_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
            metrics=script["metrics"],
            copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
            designer=designer_for(script),
            url=PROJECT_URL,
        )
        paths.append(vf_path)
        vfs[weight] = vf_path

    # COLRv1 Spectrum, Regular and Bold
    spectrum_reg = os.path.join(
        FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-SpectrumRegular.ttf"
    )
    spectrum_bold = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Spectrum.ttf")
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[400], spectrum_reg,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Regular", weight=400,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[700], spectrum_bold,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Bold", weight=700,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([spectrum_reg, spectrum_bold])

    # Static APER instances, following the Malayalam naming model.
    round_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Round.ttf")
    petal_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Petal.ttf")
    bold_petal = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-BoldPetal.ttf")
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], round_static, {"APER": 0},
        f"{script['family']} Round", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], petal_static, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[700], bold_petal, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Bold",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([round_static, petal_static, bold_petal])

    for path in paths:
        to_woff2(path)
    print(f"{key}: wrote {len(paths)} TTF + WOFF2 files")
    return paths


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument(
        "scripts", nargs="*", choices=sorted(SCRIPTS),
        help="script families to build (default: all)",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    selected = args.scripts or list(SCRIPTS)
    for key in selected:
        build_script(key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate Ezhuthu Kamalam specimen / proof images.

Outputs (proofs/):
  kamalam_hero.png       — dark Sarvam-inspired hero poster
  kamalam_axis.png       — the APER axis, 0 → 100
  kamalam_gradient.png   — spectrum text block
  kamalam_spectrum.png   — gradient wordmark
  kamalam_glyphs.png     — monochrome character sheet
"""
import math
import os
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter, ImageFont
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from render import render_alpha  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
FONTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "fonts")
PROOFS = os.path.join(ROOT, "proofs")
TMP = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ezhuthu_specimen")
os.makedirs(TMP, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(PROOFS, exist_ok=True)

REG = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf")
BOLD = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Bold.ttf")
SPECTRUM = os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-Spectrum.ttf")

DEJAVU = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf"
DEJAVU_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf"

# Sarvam-adjacent spectrum: indigo → blue → periwinkle → violet → pink → orange → gold
STOPS = [
    (0.00, (24, 30, 92)),
    (0.18, (43, 63, 176)),
    (0.38, (92, 100, 219)),
    (0.56, (160, 108, 210)),
    (0.72, (217, 115, 160)),
    (0.86, (238, 121, 68)),
    (1.00, (249, 195, 109)),
]


def rgb(c):
    return tuple(int(v) for v in c)


def gradient_array(w, h, stops=STOPS, y0=None, y1=None):
    if y0 is None:
        y0 = 0
    if y1 is None:
        y1 = h
    arr = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    for y in range(h):
        t = (y - y0) / max(1, (y1 - y0))
        t = min(1.0, max(0.0, t))
        for i in range(len(stops) - 1):
            p0, c0 = stops[i]
            p1, c1 = stops[i + 1]
            if p0 <= t <= p1:
                u = (t - p0) / max(1e-9, p1 - p0)
                arr[y, :, 0] = c0[0] + (c1[0] - c0[0]) * u
                arr[y, :, 1] = c0[1] + (c1[1] - c0[1]) * u
                arr[y, :, 2] = c0[2] + (c1[2] - c0[2]) * u
                break
    return arr


def gradient_image(w, h, stops=STOPS, y0=None, y1=None):
    arr = gradient_array(w, h, stops, y0, y1)
    return Image.fromarray(arr.astype(np.uint8), "RGB")


def glow_background(w, h):
    # deep vertical gradient
    base = gradient_array(w, h, [
        (0.0, (5, 7, 16)),
        (0.35, (12, 14, 38)),
        (0.68, (28, 15, 48)),
        (1.0, (48, 17, 28)),
    ])
    Y, X = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float32)
    for cx, cy, rx, ry, color, strength in [
        (0.50 * w, 0.82 * h, 0.62 * w, 0.40 * h, (238, 121, 68), 0.30),
        (0.24 * w, 0.18 * h, 0.45 * w, 0.40 * h, (60, 84, 220), 0.22),
        (0.82 * w, 0.30 * h, 0.35 * w, 0.35 * h, (120, 72, 190), 0.16),
    ]:
        d = np.sqrt(((X - cx) / rx) ** 2 + ((Y - cy) / ry) ** 2)
        m = np.exp(-d * d * 2.6)[..., None]
        base += np.array(color, dtype=np.float32) * m * strength
    # subtle grain
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    base += rng.normal(0, 2.0, base.shape)
    return Image.fromarray(np.clip(base, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8), "RGB")


def ink_alpha(font_path, text, size, pad=40):
    alpha, baseline = render_alpha(font_path, text, size=size, pad=pad)
    return alpha, baseline


def bbox_alpha(alpha):
    return alpha.getbbox()


def gradient_text(font_path, text, size, stops=STOPS, pad=40, glow=0):
    alpha, baseline = ink_alpha(font_path, text, size, pad)
    if alpha is None:
        return None, 0, 0
    bbox = alpha.getbbox()
    if bbox is None:
        return None, 0, 0
    grad = gradient_image(alpha.width, alpha.height, stops, bbox[1], bbox[3])
    layer = grad.convert("RGBA")
    layer.putalpha(alpha)
    if glow:
        gl = alpha.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(glow))
        gl_img = gradient_image(alpha.width, alpha.height, stops, bbox[1], bbox[3])
        gl_layer = gl_img.convert("RGBA")
        a = np.array(gl, dtype=np.float32) * 0.55
        gl_layer.putalpha(Image.fromarray(a.astype(np.uint8)))
        out = Image.new("RGBA", (alpha.width, alpha.height), (0, 0, 0, 0))
        out.alpha_composite(gl_layer)
        out.alpha_composite(layer)
        return out, baseline, alpha.getbbox()
    return layer, baseline, alpha.getbbox()


def paste_center(canvas, layer, cx, baseline=None, top=None):
    x = int(cx - layer.width / 2)
    y = int((baseline - 0) - layer.height) if top is None else int(top)
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (x, y))
    return x, y


def paste_at_baseline(canvas, layer, x, baseline, baseline_in_layer):
    y = int(baseline - baseline_in_layer)
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (int(x), y))
    return int(x), y


def draw_label(draw, text, xy, size=20, color=(220, 225, 255), bold=False,
               tracking=0):
    font = ImageFont.truetype(DEJAVU_BOLD if bold else DEJAVU, size)
    x, y = xy
    if tracking:
        for ch in text:
            draw.text((x, y), ch, font=font, fill=color)
            x += draw.textlength(ch, font=font) + tracking
    else:
        draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=color)
    return draw


def draw_rule(draw, x0, y0, x1, y1, color=(255, 255, 255, 30), width=1):
    draw.line([(x0, y0), (x1, y1)], fill=color, width=width)


def instantiate_aper(src, aper):
    out = os.path.join(TMP, f"aper{int(aper)}.ttf")
    f = TTFont(src)
    instantiateVariableFont(f, {"APER": aper}, inplace=True)
    f.save(out)
    return out


def solid_text(font_path, text, size, color=(20, 20, 30, 255), pad=20):
    alpha, baseline = render_alpha(font_path, text, size=size, pad=pad)
    if alpha is None:
        return None, 0
    layer = Image.new("RGBA", (alpha.width, alpha.height), color[:3] + (255,))
    layer.putalpha(alpha)
    return layer, baseline


def paste_text(canvas, font_path, text, size, x, baseline, color=(20, 20, 30),
               pad=20):
    layer, b = solid_text(font_path, text, size, color + (255,) if len(color) == 3 else color, pad)
    if layer is None:
        return
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (int(x), int(baseline - b)))


def paste_text_right(canvas, font_path, text, size, right, baseline, color=(20, 20, 30)):
    layer, b = solid_text(font_path, text, size, color + (255,) if len(color) == 3 else color)
    if layer is None:
        return
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (int(right - layer.width), int(baseline - b)))


def _cubic(p0, p1, p2, p3, t):
    mt = 1 - t
    return (
        mt ** 3 * p0[0] + 3 * mt * mt * t * p1[0] + 3 * mt * t * t * p2[0] + t ** 3 * p3[0],
        mt ** 3 * p0[1] + 3 * mt * mt * t * p1[1] + 3 * mt * t * t * p2[1] + t ** 3 * p3[1],
    )


def teardrop_pts(cx, cy, rx, ry, cusp=20, n=40):
    """Smooth petal outline in PIL coordinates (y grows down): round base,
    pointed crown at the top."""
    p0 = (cx, cy + ry)                 # round base (lower on screen)
    p1 = (cx + rx, cy)                 # right
    tip = (cx, cy - ry - cusp)         # pointed crown (higher on screen)
    p3 = (cx - rx, cy)                 # left
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / n
        pts.append(_cubic(p0, (cx + rx * 0.62, cy + ry), (cx + rx, cy + ry * 0.62), p1, t))
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / n
        pts.append(_cubic(p1, (cx + rx, cy - ry * 0.42), (cx + rx * 0.55, tip[1] + ry * 0.12), tip, t))
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / n

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the multiscript specimen images.

Outputs (proofs/):
  kamalam_multiscript.png       — five-script hero poster
  kamalam_multiscript_axis.png  — the APER axis across four scripts
  kamalam_devanagari.png        — Devanagari sheet
  kamalam_tamil.png             — Tamil sheet
  kamalam_telugu.png            — Telugu sheet
  kamalam_kannada.png           — Kannada sheet
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from specimen import (  # noqa: E402
    DEJAVU,
    DEJAVU_BOLD,
    PROOFS,
    STOPS,
    add_mandala,
    draw_label,
    draw_rule,
    glow_background,
    gradient_text,
    paste_center,
    paste_text,
    solid_text,
)
from multiscript import SCRIPTS  # noqa: E402

FONTS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(PROOFS), "fonts")
TMP = os.path.join(PROOFS, "..", "sources", "masters")
os.makedirs(TMP, exist_ok=True)

PAPER = (247, 243, 235, 255)
INK = (28, 26, 30)
MUTED = (120, 110, 100)
ORANGE = (238, 121, 68)
BLUE = (43, 63, 176)


def font_path(stem, style):
    return os.path.join(FONTS, f"{stem}-{style}.ttf")


def instantiate_script(stem, weight, aper, tag=""):
    src = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{stem}-{'Bold' if weight >= 700 else 'Regular'}.ttf")
    out = os.path.join(TMP, f"{stem}-{weight}-aper{int(aper)}{tag}.ttf")
    font = TTFont(src)
    instantiateVariableFont(font, {"APER": aper}, inplace=True)
    font.save(out)
    return out


def paper_background(w, h):
    bg = Image.new("RGBA", (w, h), PAPER)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(19)
    grain = rng.normal(0, 1.6, (h, w, 1))
    arr = np.clip(np.array(bg)[:, :, :3] + grain, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return Image.fromarray(arr, "RGB").convert("RGBA")


def paste_solid(canvas, font, text, size, x, baseline, color=INK, pad=20):
    layer, b = solid_text(font, text, size, color=color + (255,), pad=pad)
    if layer is None:
        return
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (int(x), int(baseline - b)))


def gradient_paste(canvas, font, text, size, x, baseline, stops=STOPS,
                   glow=0, pad=24):
    layer, b, _ = gradient_text(font, text, size, stops=stops, pad=pad, glow=glow)
    if layer is None:
        return
    canvas.alpha_composite(layer, (int(x), int(baseline - b)))


def script_display(script):
    return " ".join(script["display"][:2])


def make_hero():
    W, H = 1600, 1900
    bg = glow_background(W, H).convert("RGBA")
    add_mandala(bg, W / 2, 260, 360, petals=28, alpha=14, width=1)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(bg)
    draw_label(d, "EZHUTHU KAMALAM", (90, 80), 20, (205, 215, 255),
               bold=True, tracking=5)
    draw_label(d, "MULTISCRIPT  /  ONE APERTURE", (90, 116), 14,
               (145, 160, 200), tracking=4)
    draw_label(d, "APER 0 → 100", (W - 300, 80), 16, (255, 210, 170),
               bold=True)
    draw_rule(d, 90, 164, W - 90, 164, (255, 255, 255, 28))

    # Malayalam stays the reference row, then the four new scripts.
    rows = [
        ("മലയാളം", "MALAYALAM", "MLYM",
         os.path.join(FONTS, "EzhuthuKamalam-BoldPetal.ttf"), "എഴുത്ത് കമലം"),
    ]
    for key, script in SCRIPTS.items():
        rows.append((
            {
                "devanagari": "देवनागरी", "tamil": "தமிழ்",
                "telugu": "తెలుగు", "kannada": "ಕನ್ನಡ",
            }[key],
            key.upper(),
            {"devanagari": "DEVA", "tamil": "TAML",
             "telugu": "TELU", "kannada": "KNDA"}[key],
            font_path(script["stem"], "BoldPetal"),
            script_display(script),
        ))

    y = 260
    for name, label, code, path, text in rows:
        draw_label(d, label, (90, y - 10), 13, (150, 165, 205),
                   bold=True, tracking=3)
        draw_label(d, code, (90, y + 14), 11, (238, 140, 100), tracking=2)
        paste_solid(bg, path, name, 34, 90, y + 92, (200, 208, 232))
        gradient_paste(bg, path, text, 132, 300, y + 80,
                       stops=[(0, (255, 246, 232)), (1, (255, 205, 160))],
                       glow=10)
        y += 290
        if y < 1650:
            draw_rule(d, 90, y - 40, W - 90, y - 40, (255, 255, 255, 22))

    draw_rule(d, 90, H - 130, W - 90, H - 130, (255, 255, 255, 30))
    draw_label(d, "EZHUTHU KAMALAM  /  v1.100  /  OFL 1.1", (90, H - 100),
               14, (150, 162, 195), tracking=1)
    draw_label(d, "MALAYALAM  ·  DEVANAGARI  ·  TAMIL  ·  TELUGU  ·  KANNADA",
               (90, H - 74), 12, (190, 170, 150), tracking=1)
    draw_label(d, "A type system that blooms.", (W - 330, H - 100), 16,
               (255, 235, 220))
    bg.convert("RGB").save(os.path.join(PROOFS, "kamalam_multiscript.png"))
    print("multiscript hero")


def make_axis():
    W, H = 1600, 1160
    bg = glow_background(W, H).convert("RGBA")
    bg = Image.blend(bg, Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (8, 10, 22, 255)), 0.55)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(bg)
    draw_label(d, "THE APERTURE AXIS", (90, 78), 20, (210, 220, 255),
               bold=True, tracking=4)
    draw_label(d, "ROUND  →  BLOOM  →  PETAL", (90, 112), 13,
               (150, 165, 205), tracking=3)
    draw_label(d, "APER 0 — 100", (W - 280, 80), 15, (255, 210, 170),
               bold=True)

    values = [0, 25, 50, 75, 100]
    rows = [
        ("devanagari", "क", "DEVANAGARI"),
        ("tamil", "ண", "TAMIL"),
        ("telugu", "క", "TELUGU"),
        ("kannada", "ಕ", "KANNADA"),
    ]
    left = 330
    colw = (W - left - 80) / len(values)
    top = 230
    rowh = 205
    for j, v in enumerate(values):
        x = left + j * colw + colw / 2
        draw_label(d, f"{v:03d}", (int(x - 18), 180), 14, (238, 140, 100),
                   bold=True)
        draw_label(d, "ROUND" if v == 0 else "PETAL" if v == 100 else "",
                   (int(x - 28), 202), 9, (125, 140, 180), tracking=2)
    draw_rule(d, 90, 222, W - 90, 222, (255, 255, 255, 26))

    for i, (key, glyph, label) in enumerate(rows):
        script = SCRIPTS[key]
        y = top + i * rowh
        draw_label(d, label, (90, y + 80), 13, (150, 165, 205),
                   bold=True, tracking=3)
        draw_label(d, {"devanagari": "देवनागरी", "tamil": "தமிழ்",
                       "telugu": "తెలుగు", "kannada": "ಕನ್ನಡ"}[key],
                   (90, y + 102), 11, (190, 170, 150), tracking=1)
        for j, v in enumerate(values):
            p = instantiate_script(script["stem"], 700, v, tag="_axis")
            alpha, _ = __import__("render").render_alpha(p, glyph, size=128, pad=12)
            if alpha is None:
                continue
            x = int(left + j * colw + (colw - alpha.width) / 2)
            layer = Image.new("RGBA", (alpha.width, alpha.height),
                              (248, 241, 228, 255))
            layer.putalpha(alpha)
            bg.alpha_composite(layer, (x, int(y + 20)))
        if i < len(rows) - 1:
            draw_rule(d, 90, y + rowh - 18, W - 90, y + rowh - 18,
                      (255, 255, 255, 18))
    draw_label(d, "Ezhuthu Kamalam  /  the same axis in four scripts",
               (90, H - 60), 12, (150, 162, 195))
    bg.convert("RGB").save(os.path.join(PROOFS, "kamalam_multiscript_axis.png"))
    print("multiscript axis")


def make_sheet(key):
    script = SCRIPTS[key]
    stem = script["stem"]
    display = script["display"]
    rep = {
        "devanagari": "क", "tamil": "ண",
        "telugu": "క", "kannada": "ಕ",
    }[key]
    script_name = {
        "devanagari": "देवनागरी", "tamil": "தமிழ்",
        "telugu": "తెలుగు", "kannada": "ಕನ್ನಡ",
    }[key]
    W, H = 1600, 1120
    bg = paper_background(W, H)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(bg)
    draw_label(d, f"EZHUTHU KAMALAM  /  {key.upper()}", (80, 62), 13,
               (150, 110, 70), bold=True, tracking=2)
    draw_rule(d, 80, 96, W - 80, 96, (30, 30, 30, 40))
    draw_label(d, "APER 0 — 100", (W - 250, 62), 13, (150, 110, 70),
               bold=True, tracking=2)

    # large display word
    gradient_paste(bg, font_path(stem, "BoldPetal"), display[0], 250,
                   80, 390, stops=[(0, (20, 24, 40)), (1, (120, 50, 35))],
                   pad=40)
    # the script's own name, in its own script
    paste_solid(bg, font_path(stem, "Petal"), script_name, 44, 80, 470,
                (120, 80, 50))
    # second display word
    paste_solid(bg, font_path(stem, "BoldPetal"), display[1], 110,
                80, 600, (28, 26, 30))
    # paragraph
    y = 700
    for line in script["paragraph"]:
        paste_solid(bg, font_path(stem, "Petal"), line, 30, 80, y,
                    (55, 50, 45))
        y += 46

    # APER strip
    strip_y = 820
    draw_label(d, "THE APER STRIP", (80, strip_y - 28), 11, (150, 110, 70),
               bold=True, tracking=2)
    for j, v in enumerate((0, 25, 50, 75, 100)):
        p = instantiate_script(stem, 700, v, tag="_sheet")
        alpha, _ = __import__("render").render_alpha(p, rep, size=92, pad=10)
        if alpha is None:
            continue
        x = 80 + j * 300
        layer = Image.new("RGBA", (alpha.width, alpha.height),
                          (28, 26, 30, 255))
        layer.putalpha(alpha)
        bg.alpha_composite(layer, (x, strip_y))
        draw_label(d, f"{v:03d}", (x, strip_y + 120), 12, (238, 121, 68),
                   bold=True)
        draw_label(d, "ROUND" if v == 0 else "PETAL" if v == 100 else "",
                   (x, strip_y + 140), 9, (140, 120, 100), tracking=2)

    # spectrum sample
    draw_label(d, "SPECTRUM  /  COLRv1", (W - 500, 740), 11, (150, 110, 70),
               bold=True, tracking=2)
    gradient_paste(bg, font_path(stem, "BoldPetal"), display[0], 90,
                   W - 500, 850, stops=STOPS, glow=6)

    draw_rule(d, 80, H - 90, W - 80, H - 90, (30, 30, 30, 36))
    draw_label(d, f"{script['family']}  /  OFL 1.1  /  base: Noto Sans "
               f"{ {'devanagari':'Devanagari','tamil':'Tamil','telugu':'Telugu','kannada':'Kannada'}[key] }",
               (80, H - 70), 11, (150, 130, 110))
    bg.convert("RGB").save(os.path.join(PROOFS, f"kamalam_{key}.png"))
    print(f"{key} sheet")


def main():
    which = sys.argv[1:] or ["hero", "axis", "devanagari", "tamil",
                             "telugu", "kannada"]
    if "hero" in which:
        make_hero()
    if "axis" in which:
        make_axis()
    for key in ("devanagari", "tamil", "telugu", "kannada"):
        if key in which:
            make_sheet(key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print an HTML specimen to a vector PDF with Chromium.

Requires Playwright + Chromium:
    .venv/bin/pip install playwright
    .venv/bin/python -m playwright install chromium

Usage:
    python tools/pdf.py [input.html] [output.pdf]
"""
import argparse
import os

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DEFAULT_HTML = os.path.join(ROOT, "specimen", "index.html")
DEFAULT_OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "proofs", "EzhuthuKamalam-Specimen.pdf")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("input", nargs="?", default=DEFAULT_HTML)
    ap.add_argument("output", nargs="?", default=DEFAULT_OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1600, "height": 1000})
        page.goto("file://" + os.path.abspath(args.input))
        page.wait_for_timeout(3000)  # let fonts load and the bloom finish
        height = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollHeight")
        page.pdf(
            path=args.output,
            width="1600px",
            height=f"{height}px",
            print_background=True,
            margin={"top": "0", "bottom": "0", "left": "0", "right": "0"},
        )
        browser.close()
    print("wrote", args.output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1: Ezhuthu Kamalam Font Family
2: ===========================
3: 
4: ![Ezhuthu Kamalam — a Malayalam typeface that blooms](proofs/kamalam_hero.png)
5: 
6: **Ezhuthu Kamalam** is a Malayalam display typeface that treats the script's
7: loops as thresholds. Malayalam is a script of round counters and open curls;
8: Kamalam turns each one into a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable
9: axis the loop is the classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a
10: soft petal. The transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real
11: OpenType variation axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.
12: 
13: The family was designed for the large gesture: headlines, wordmarks, posters,
14: title cards, brand systems and screens where Malayalam should feel
15: contemporary without losing its roots. It is also comfortable in text, where
16: the petal crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.
17: 
18: The typeface is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh Thottingal and
19: Swathanthra Malayalam Computing, used under the SIL Open Font License. The
20: aperture engine, variable axis, spectrum build, metrics and specimens are new
21: work by the Ezhuthu Project Authors.

23: The Aperture Axis
24: -----------------
25: 
26: ![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kamalam_axis.png)
27: 
28: Every counter in Ezhuthu Kamalam can open from a classic round loop
29: (`APER 0`) to a pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis is exposed as
30: `APER` in the variable fonts and has five named stops:
31: 
32: | APER | Name | Character |
33: |---:|---|---|
34: | 0 | Round | The classic Manjari loop |
35: | 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
36: | 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
37: | 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
38: | 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |
39:

44: changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the

Ezhuthu Kamalam Multiscript Font Family
=======================================

![Five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kamalam_multiscript.png)

**Ezhuthu Kamalam** is a multiscript display type system built around one
idea: the counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a
loop is the classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft
petal. The transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType
variation axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.

The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
**Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of named
stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.

The Malayalam branch is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh
Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. The four new branches are
built on the corresponding **Noto Sans** skeletons by the Noto Project
Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
the Ezhuthu Project Authors.

Five Scripts, One Aperture
--------------------------

| Script | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Malayalam | `Ezhuthu Kamalam` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
| Devanagari (Hindi) | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
| Tamil | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
| Telugu | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
| Kannada | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |

“Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.

![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kamalam_multiscript_axis.png)

Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
single counter grammar:

- **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
  headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
- **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
  more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and the inner curves.
- **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
  loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
- The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
  punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
  the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.

The per-script specimens show the full system:

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Devanagari](proofs/kamalam_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kamalam_tamil.png) |
| ![Telugu](proofs/kamalam_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kamalam_kannada.png) |

The Aperture Axis
-----------------

![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kamalam_axis.png)

Every counter in Ezhuthu Kamalam can open from a classic round loop
(`APER 0`) to a pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis is exposed as
`APER` in every variable font and has five named stops:

| APER | Name | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Round | The classic loop |
| 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
| 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
| 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |

![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kamalam_aper.gif)

The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
kerning.

The Spectrum
------------

![Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum](proofs/kamalam_gradient.png)

**Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font
itself with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline
and gold in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field
rather than a set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum
builds ship for every script.

The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
[Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.

In Context
----------

The same fonts, the same axis, the same spectrum — applied to the kinds of
surfaces a contemporary Indian type system has to live on.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Poster](proofs/kamalam_poster.png) | ![Editorial spread](proofs/kamalam_editorial.png) |
| ![Product UI](proofs/kamalam_ui.png) | ![Social card](proofs/kamalam_social.png) |

![Ezhuthu Kamalam lockup](proofs/kamalam_lockup.png)

Character Set
-------------

![Ezhuthu Kamalam character sheet](proofs/kamalam_glyphs.png)

The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:

- 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
- Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
- Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
- Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
- Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
- **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold

The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
bases: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended and the
Vedic extensions supported by Noto; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada include their
full blocks. Coverage is verified codepoint by codepoint in
`tests/test_multiscript.py`.

The Family
----------

The Malayalam family:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Bold.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Spectrum.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold + COLRv1 spectrum |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-SpectrumRegular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular + COLRv1 spectrum |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Round.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 0` instance |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Petal.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 100` instance |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-BoldPetal.ttf/.woff2` | Static Bold `APER 100` instance |

Each new script ships the same seven styles:

| Family | Files |
|---|---|
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamDevanagari-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamTamil-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamTelugu-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamKannada-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |

Specimens:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `specimen/index.html` | Interactive Malayalam specimen (fonts embedded) |
| `specimen/multiscript.html` | Interactive five-script specimen with a shared APER slider |
| `proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Specimen.pdf` | Vector Malayalam PDF specimen |
| `proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf` | Vector multiscript PDF specimen |

Downloading the font files
--------------------------

The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
vector PDF is
[`proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:

```bash
make serve   # http://localhost:8000
```

Using the font
--------------

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari";
  src: url("EzhuthuKamalamDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
}

.deva {
  font-family: "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari";
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
}
```

```python
# HarfBuzz / uharfbuzz
font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
```

For mixed-script copy, stack the families. The browser picks the first family
that supports each character; the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the
shared Latin, and the script families fill in the rest:

```css
.multiscript {
  font-family:
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada",
    sans-serif;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

For the colour builds, use `EzhuthuKamalam<Script>-SpectrumRegular` or
`EzhuthuKamalam<Script>-Spectrum`. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.

Building from source
--------------------

The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1:

```bash
make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
make kamalam         # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
```

Sources live in `sources/base/` (Manjari and the four Noto Sans variable
skeletons). The aperture engine is `tools/kamalam.py`; the multiscript driver
is `tools/multiscript.py`. The build is reproducible: repeated runs produce
byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. Design and engineering notes are in
[NOTES.md](NOTES.md).

Testing and QA
--------------

- HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
  glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
- Full cmap coverage of each base script, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
  and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the base.
- Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
  untouched in the script families.
- Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
  names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.
- Fontbakery universal: **0 FAIL** on all eight multiscript Regular/Bold
  variable fonts (the same documented custom-axis, STAT-name-length and
  Bold/`fsSelection` exclusions as Malayalam; inherited Noto warnings are
  listed in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md)).
- Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
  Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
- Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kamalam` and `make multiscript`.

Bug reports, glyph requests and feature suggestions are welcome. Open an
issue in the repository or send a pull request against the `tools/` and

## 6. Testing

`tests/test_kamalam.py` checks:

- `fvar` axis `APER = 0…100`, default 100;
- `STAT` axis values Round / Bloom / Petal;
- the OFL name table and Manjari attribution on every build;
- shaping of 35+ Malayalam strings at `APER 0`, `50`, `100`, with identical
  glyph sequences;
- coverage of every assigned Malayalam codepoint;
- outline variation between the extremes;
- COLR/CPAL structure, 907 paint records and 7 palette entries.

The HTML specimen was also checked in headless Chromium 156: the embedded
variable fonts load, the APER slider changes the live instance, and the
`Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum` sample paints its COLRv1 gradient in the browser.

Builds are reproducible: `head.created`/`head.modified` are pinned to a fixed
date and `recalcTimestamp` is disabled, so repeated `make kamalam` runs produce
byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is deterministic too.

The old `tests/test_font.py` still covers the legacy draft.

## 7. Fontbakery notes

The Regular font passes `fontbakery check-universal` with two exclusions that
do not apply to this design:

- `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` assumes a registered `wght`/`wdth`
  axis; Ezhuthu Kamalam's only axis is the custom `APER`.
- `alt_caron` is a Czech/Slovak-specific check that wants `ď` to use a
  non-standard caron glyph. The Latin `ď` here uses a combining caron, which
  is typographically correct; the check is not relevant to a Malayalam face.

For the Bold and Spectrum builds, `opentype/fsselection` and
`opentype/mac_style` also need excluding because fontbakery infers "Bold"
from a `wght` axis or a filename convention and cannot see the custom-axis
Bold style; the OS/2 and `head` values themselves are correct. Run the QA
target with:

```bash
make qa
```

The specimen HTML and COLRv1 paint were verified in headless Chromium 156.

## 8. Known limits / next work

- The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
  construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
  from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
- The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
  would be the next step.
- A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
  (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
- The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
  smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.

## 8. Known limits / next work

- The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
  construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
  from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
- The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
  would be the next step.
- A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
  (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
- The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
  smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.

## 9. The multiscript extension

### 9.1 Why separate families

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face; it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada glyphs. A literal Manjari derivative therefore cannot cover those
scripts. The multiscript release uses one OFL skeleton per script and keeps the
same derivative model: rename, preserve the upstream copyright, record the
base, and do the new work in the aperture engine, axis, Spectrum, metrics and
specimens.

The four new families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
attachments and vertical metrics; merging them would create conflicts in
shared Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
line height.

### 9.2 Sources

| Branch | Base | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
| Tamil | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
| Telugu | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
| Kannada | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |

The variable bases are instantiated at `wght=400/700`, `wdth=100`, scaled to
1000 UPM (they are already 1000), stripped of hinting and variation tables, and
given the Ezhuthu name/metrics. The vendored files and SHA-256 checksums are in
`sources/base/README.md`.

### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles

The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the
scripts do not share one counter grammar.

| Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open |
| Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
| Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
| Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |

`PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction),
`freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and
`valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam
build remains byte-identical.

The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base
letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the
headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can
rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first
attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled
the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower
`sigma_f=0.22` fixed it.

### 9.4 Glyph filtering

`petal_warp` accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. `tools/multiscript.py`
computes that set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's
codepoints and closes over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms,
contextual variants and matras are included. Latin, punctuation and unrelated
glyphs are left in the base style. This is why the Latin in the new families
stays Noto Sans, while the script outline changes.

The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.

### 9.5 Metrics

The new families use the base typographic ascender/descender, but the win
metrics are computed from the actual outline extents:

```
usWinAscent  = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50)
usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50)
```

Devanagari uses `sTypoAscender=1000` (rather than Noto's 896) because its
Vedic marks reach y=1347 and fontbakery's ascender check wants more room. The
other families keep their base ascenders: Tamil 870, Telugu 869, Kannada 809.
All set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`.

### 9.6 Testing and QA

`tests/test_multiscript.py` checks, for all four scripts:

- `fvar` `APER=0…100`, default 100, and STAT values 0/50/100;
- the Noto copyright and Ezhuthu modification notice in name ID 0, the Noto
  designer credit in name ID 9, and the OFL notice in name ID 13;
- shaping of every case, display word and paragraph at APER 0/50/100, with
  identical glyph names and advances and no `.notdef`;
- full cmap coverage of the base script, and shaping every script codepoint
  (marks with a base consonant);
- outline variation between APER 0 and 100, and a guard that Latin `H` is
  unchanged;
- static Round/Petal instances, names and the fact that they differ;
- COLRv1/CPAL structure in both Spectrum builds.

Fontbakery `check-universal` reports **0 FAIL** on all eight new Regular/Bold
VFs. The exclusions are the same as Malayalam:

- `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` (custom `APER` axis);
- `alt_caron` (Czech/Slovak-specific);
- `opentype/fsselection` and `opentype/mac_style` for Bold (fontbakery infers
  "Regular" from the custom axis and cannot see the Bold style, although the
  OS/2 and `head` bits are correct).

The STAT value labels for the new families are `0`, `50`, `100` rather than
`Round`, `Bloom`, `Petal`: the family name plus the poetic label would exceed
Microsoft's 31-character family+style limit. The `fvar` named instances keep
the poetic names, and the specimen and documentation use them.

Inherited Noto warnings (not introduced by this project) include:

- GDEF mark-class warnings for Vedic characters;
- a missing `avar` table (the APER axis is linear, so no mapping is needed);
- long Vedic glyph names and unreachable Vedic variants;
- a soft hyphen in the base font.

These are recorded rather than silenced, because changing GDEF classes or
removing Vedic glyphs could break shaping.

### 9.7 Multiscript limits

- Tamil has fewer closed counters than the other scripts, so its APER change
  is deliberately subtler. A more radical Tamil cut would need new stroke
  terminals, not just a counter warp.
- The four families are separate fonts. A merged all-in-one font is not
  planned because of the shaping and glyph-name conflicts described above.
- The Spectrum gradient is the same font-unit range for every script; a
  per-script baseline calibration could be a future refinement.

The aperture engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are Copyright 2026 The Kallar Project Authors. The legacy v0.2 from-scratch parametric draft is preserved in [`legacy/`](legacy/) and in `tools/glyphs_ml.py`. Credits ------- - **Design, aperture engine, variable fonts, Spectrum, specimens:** Ezhuthu Project Authors - **Malayalam base skeleton:** Santhosh Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing - **Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada base skeletons:** The Noto Project Authors - **Legacy v0.2 shaping engine:** adapted from [Nupuram](https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/Nupuram) by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC (MIT) - **Sarvam inspiration:** the blue → orange spectrum and the gateway/lotus language are an homage to [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand) Getting involved ---------------- Bug reports, glyph requests and feature suggestions are welcome. Open an issue in the repository or send a pull request against the `tools/` and `sources/` directories. Please run `make test` and `make qa-multiscript` before sending a contribution. If you use Kallar in a project, a small credit — “Typeface: Ezhuthu Kallar” — is appreciated. ---NOTES--- | Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari | | Tamil | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil | | Telugu | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu | | Kannada | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada | The variable bases are instantiated at `wght=400/700`, `wdth=100`, scaled to 1000 UPM (they are already 1000), stripped of hinting and variation tables, and given the Ezhuthu name/metrics. The vendored files and SHA-256 checksums are in `sources/base/README.md`. ### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the scripts do not share one counter grammar. | Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes | |---|---:|---:|---|---:|---| | Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open | | Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops | | Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp | | Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp | `PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction), `freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and `valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam build remains byte-identical. The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower `sigma_f=0.22` fixed it. ### 9.4 Glyph filtering `petal_warp` accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. `tools/multiscript.py` computes that set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's codepoints and closes over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms, contextual variants and matras are included. Latin, punctuation and unrelated glyphs are left in the base style. This is why the Latin in the new families stays Noto Sans, while the script outline changes. The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723 Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs. ### 9.5 Metrics The new families use the base typographic ascender/descender, but the win metrics are computed from the actual outline extents: ``` usWinAscent = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50) usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50) ``` Devanagari uses `sTypoAscender=1000` (rather than Noto's 896) because its Vedic marks reach y=1347 and fontbakery's ascender check wants more room. The other families keep their base ascenders: Tamil 870, Telugu 869, Kannada 809. All set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`. ### 9.6 Testing and QA `tests/test_multiscript.py` checks, for all four scripts: - `fvar` `APER=0…100`, default 100, and STAT values 0/50/100; - the Noto copyright and Ezhuthu modification notice in name ID 0, the Noto designer credit in name ID 9, and the OFL notice in name ID 13; - shaping of every case, display word and paragraph at APER 0/50/100, with identical glyph names and advances and no `.notdef`; - full cmap coverage of the base script, and shaping every script codepoint (marks with a base consonant); - outline variation between APER 0 and 100, and a guard that Latin `H` is ---HTML footer--- ScriptsMalayalam, Latin FormatTTF · WOFF2

.PHONY: help venv kamalam multiscript legacy test proofs specimen serve clean distclean \
	pdf pdf-multiscript qa qa-multiscript

PY := .venv/bin/python
PIP := .venv/bin/pip

help:
	@echo "targets:"
	@echo "  venv      create .venv and install build/proof dependencies"
	@echo "  kamalam   build the variable Kallar family + Spectrum"
	@echo "  multiscript build Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families"
	@echo "  legacy    rebuild the v0.2 parametric draft (legacy/fonts)"
	@echo "  test      run shaping, variation and colour tests"
	@echo "  proofs    render the specimen PNGs and the HTML specimen"
	@echo "  pdf       print the specimen to proofs/Kallar-Specimen.pdf"
	@echo "  pdf-multiscript print the multiscript specimen to PDF"
	@echo "  qa        run fontbakery on the Malayalam Regular and Bold"
	@echo "  qa-multiscript run fontbakery on the four script families"
	@echo "  specimen  alias for proofs"
	@echo "  serve     serve specimen/ on http://localhost:8000"
	@echo "  clean     remove generated UFOs and masters"
	@echo "  distclean remove generated fonts and proofs too"

venv:
	test -d .venv || { python3 -m venv .venv; $(PIP) install -U pip; }
	$(PIP) install -q ufoLib2 ufo2ft fonttools fontFeatures munch PyYAML \
		uharfbuzz freetype-py pillow booleanOperations Brotli scipy

kamalam: venv
	$(PY) tools/kallar.py all

multiscript: venv
	$(PY) tools/multiscript.py

legacy: venv
	$(PY) tools/build.py

test: venv kamalam multiscript
	$(PY) tests/test_kallar.py
	$(PY) tests/test_multiscript.py
	@if test -f legacy/fonts/Ezhuthu-Regular.ttf; then \
		$(PY) tests/test_font.py legacy/fonts/Ezhuthu-Regular.ttf; \
	else \
		echo "legacy font not built; run: make legacy"; \
	fi

proofs: kamalam multiscript
	$(PY) tools/specimen.py

	$(PY) tools/pdf.py

qa: kamalam
	$(PIP) install -q fontbakery
	$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal fonts/Kallar-Regular.ttf \
		--no-progress -x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron
	$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal fonts/Kallar-Bold.ttf \
		--no-progress -x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron \
		-x opentype/fsselection -x opentype/mac_style

qa-multiscript: multiscript
	$(PIP) install -q fontbakery
	@for f in \
		fonts/KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarDevanagari-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTamil-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTamil-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTelugu-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTelugu-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarKannada-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarKannada-Bold.ttf; do \
		echo "== $$f"; \
		$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal "$$f" --no-progress \
			-x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron \
			-x opentype/fsselection -x opentype/mac_style \
			2>&1 | grep -E '^    (FAIL|WARN|PASS):|^Total:' | tail -5; \
	done

specimen: proofs
	@echo "open specimen/index.html in a browser (or run: make serve)"

serve: specimen

clean:

distclean: clean
	rm -rf fonts/*.ttf fonts/*.otf fonts/*.woff2 proofs/kallar_*.png \
		proofs/Kallar-Specimen.pdf \
		proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf
